questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern since it is stopped.
Is only a concern if passengers are getting off the bus.
Is always a concern, whether you can see passengers or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is always a concern, whether you can see passengers or not.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when driving near a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby. The bus can block their view of you or your view of them.

questions.question: A sign showing a maximum safe speed:

options.text: Is a suggestion. Vehicles can drive faster than the posted speed.
Only applies to vehicles weighing more than 26,000 pounds.
Must be followed. No vehicle should drive faster than the posted speed.
Only applies to cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be followed. No vehicle should drive faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: When driving, it is important to:

options.text: Avoid using your mirrors in heavy traffic.
Look only ahead and to the right.
Look ahead, to the sides, and behind your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead, to the sides, and behind your vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Look ahead and check your mirrors regularly on both sides while driving.

questions.question: Load hazardous materials:

options.text: Near heat sources.
Away from heat sources.
Away from shadows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Away from heat sources.
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Follow regulations that prohibit flammable or explosive materials from being stored with heaters.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen.
A valve that prevents the driver from speeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in a truck's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a serious leak. It closes automatically if pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?

options.text: The mechanic.
The shipper.
The driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper.
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials correctly. The driver should verify that the materials are properly labeled.

questions.question: When you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does your braking distance change?

options.text: It stays about the same.
It increases a little.
It doubles.
It quadruples (multiplies by four).

questions.correctAnswerText: It quadruples (multiplies by four).
questions.explanation: Higher speed increases your vehicle's braking distance significantly. Doubling your speed from 20 to 40 mph multiplies your braking distance by four.

questions.question: To complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest, you must:

options.text: Sign by hand.
Sign only if you cross into another state.
Sign only if the weather was dangerous.
Have a witness sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sign by hand.
questions.explanation: A Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest must be signed by hand. The manifest must also include the names and EPA registration numbers of all shippers, carriers, and destinations.

questions.question: A vehicle smaller than yours:

options.text: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
Usually takes longer to stop than your vehicle.
Takes about the same time to stop as your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can usually stop faster than your vehicle.
questions.explanation: A smaller vehicle can generally stop faster than a larger vehicle. Remember this when deciding how far to stay behind other vehicles.

questions.question: Transporting liquid cargo:

options.text: Is always easy.
Is the same as hauling solid cargo.
Is easier than transporting gas or solid cargo.
Requires special care.

questions.correctAnswerText: Requires special care.
questions.explanation: Liquid cargo in a tank vehicle requires special care. The liquid moves during transit, and the vehicle has a high center of gravity, which creates handling challenges.

questions.question: When must a written vehicle inspection report be signed?

options.text: Every day.
Only when defects are found and confirmed as repaired.
Only when repairs cost more than $1,000.
Only when a police officer asks you to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only when defects are found and confirmed as repaired.
questions.explanation: Sign the inspection report only if defects were found and confirmed as repaired or confirmed as not needing repair.

questions.question: What happens when engine belts are loose?

options.text: The water pump and fan do not work properly. This causes the engine to overheat.
The engine runs more efficiently.
The fan runs too much and the engine gets too cold.
Loose belts last longer than tight belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water pump and fan do not work properly. This causes the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check that engine belts are tight. Loose belts prevent the water pump and fan from working correctly. This can cause the engine to overheat.

questions.question: What does the suspension system do?

options.text: Supports the vehicle and its cargo.
Keeps cargo at the right distance behind the driver.
Maintains a safe distance from other vehicles.
Reduces weight on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supports the vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and its cargo while keeping the axles in place. A damaged suspension system is very dangerous.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: For parking.
Only to test the trailer brakes.
At the same time as the brake pedal.
On slippery roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve controls the trailer brakes but should only be used for testing. Using it while driving can cause a skid. Never use it while parking because it may release the air pressure that holds the brakes in place.

questions.question: When does an automatic tractor protection valve pop out?

options.text: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
When the trailer starts to jackknife.
When wheels regain traction after a skid.
When air pressure is above 45 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi.
questions.explanation: The automatic tractor protection valve pops out if air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. When it pops out, the valve closes and stops air from flowing.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of driver fatigue?

options.text: Ability to focus
Daydreaming
Repeated yawning
Drifting from your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ability to focus
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, repeated yawning or eye rubbing, daydreaming, and drifting out of your lane.

questions.question: When should a tank never be transported?

options.text: When the valves are open.
When the tank is only partially filled.
When carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the valves are open.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to transport liquids or gases in a leaking tank. Always make sure intake, discharge, and shut-off valves are in the correct positions before loading, unloading, or moving a tank.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, where should your vehicle NOT be parked?

options.text: Within 300 feet of a bridge.
Within 40 feet of the road.
In rain or snow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building (except for brief stops needed for vehicle operation). Never park within five feet of the edge of the road.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: No, they are not safe.
Yes, only on rear tires.
Yes, only when carrying heavy loads.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they are not safe.
questions.explanation: Never use wheels or rims that have been repaired by welding.

questions.question: Which tire issue does NOT need to be corrected?

options.text: Too much air pressure
Too little air pressure
Mixing radial and bias-ply tires
Tread depth of at least 4/32 inch on front tires

questions.correctAnswerText: Tread depth of at least 4/32 inch on front tires
questions.explanation: Problems to fix include: air pressure too high or too low, mixing radial and bias-ply tires, tread depth less than 4/32 inch on front tires, and tread depth less than 2/32 inch on all other tires.
